stem: Engineers reduced the ___ between the moving parts by machining the surfaces to a finer tolerance.
explanationPerOption: The purpose a thing serves. Surfaces do not have a purpose between them that machining would reduce.
A distinct part of something larger. Machining does not reduce a section.
Correct. Friction is resistance between surfaces moving over one another, and smoother surfaces reduce it.
The taking of a person by force. Shares the -ction ending but belongs to an unrelated domain.

stem: The site yielded such an ___ of pottery that cataloguing it took three seasons.
explanationPerOption: A single example of something. An instance of pottery would be one piece, which no one would spend three seasons cataloguing.
Correct. Abundance means a very large quantity, which is what makes the cataloguing take three seasons.
The management of money. Shares the -ance ending but has no quantitative sense.
A fact or condition connected to an event. It describes context, not quantity.

stem: The adaptation bears so little ___ to the novel that readers of one would not recognise the other.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Resemblance is the state of being similar, which is exactly what the second clause denies.
A fact or condition attending an event. It cannot be borne between two works.
A single occurrence or example. One does not bear an instance to something.
The management of money. Shares the ending only.

stem: The alloy was chosen because it is more ___ than steel in salt water, lasting decades without pitting.
explanationPerOption: Obtainable or at hand. Availability says nothing about lasting decades without pitting.
Large in amount or importance. It describes magnitude, not resistance to wear.
Correct. Durable means able to withstand wear over time, which the decades without pitting demonstrate.
Able to be known in advance. A predictable alloy would behave consistently, not necessarily last longer.

stem: What might have become a bitter lawsuit ended instead in an ___ settlement that both parties described as fair.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Amicable means marked by goodwill, which is what contrasts with the bitter lawsuit that was avoided.
Worthy of attention. A settlement can be remarkable without being friendly, so it misses the contrast.
Obtainable. Settlements are reached, not made obtainable.
Able to withstand wear. It applies to materials, not to the tone of an agreement.

stem: Her ___ spending drew more comment than her considerable charitable giving ever did.
explanationPerOption: Bearing on the matter at hand. Spending can be relevant to an argument, but that is not what draws comment here.
Occurring continuously. Constant spending describes frequency, not excess.
Correct. Extravagant means spending far beyond what is necessary, which is what attracts comment.
A person who lives somewhere. A noun, so it cannot modify 'spending'.

stem: He remained entirely ___ of the change until a colleague mentioned it three weeks later.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Ignorant means lacking knowledge of something, which the three-week delay establishes.
Important or meaningful. A person is not significant of something.
Bearing on the matter. A person is not relevant of a change.
Unchanging. It describes something's behaviour over time, not a person's awareness.

stem: The nest is deliberately ___: it sits in plain sight yet is almost never noticed.
explanationPerOption: Coming before in time. It cannot describe how visible something is.
Designed to attract notice. This is the exact opposite of what the colon explains.
Correct. Inconspicuous means not attracting attention, which is why the nest goes unnoticed in plain sight.
Shockingly excessive. Something outrageous would be noticed, not overlooked.

stem: The illness is ___ for several days before any symptom appears, which is what makes containment so difficult.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Contagious means transmissible by contact, and silent transmission is precisely what defeats containment.
Very large in size. An illness's size is not what containment addresses.
Careful to avoid danger. A person can be cautious; an illness cannot.
Open to more than one interpretation. It describes wording, not transmission.

stem: A convincing explanation has proved ___: each new theory accounts for some of the evidence and contradicts the rest.
explanationPerOption: Constructive, or confirming. It would suggest the explanation was found, reversing the sentence.
Offering a different possibility. The problem is that no theory works, not that several do.
Covering a wide range. An extensive explanation would be a success, not a failure.
Correct. Elusive means difficult to find or capture, which the colon then illustrates.

stem: The entire batch was recalled after ___ wiring was found in a single unit.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Defective means having a fault, which is what justifies a recall.
Covering a wide range. Extensive wiring describes quantity and would not on its own prompt a recall.
Constructive or affirmative. Positive wiring is not a fault.
Offering another option. Alternative wiring would be a design choice, not a defect.

stem: Every ___ of the design was tested separately before the parts were assembled.
explanationPerOption: A remark or observation. Remarks are not tested before assembly.
Correct. A component is a part of a larger whole, which is what gets tested before assembly.
Permission. Consent is given, not tested and assembled.
A basic constituent part. Close in meaning, but 'element' is used of abstract or chemical constituents rather than physical parts that are assembled.

stem: No treatment may proceed until the patient's written ___ has been recorded.
explanationPerOption: A remark. A recorded remark does not authorise treatment.
Correct. Consent is permission granted, which is the legal precondition for treatment.
A part of a larger whole. Patients do not give components.
A written record. Close, since consent is often documented, but the document is the vehicle and the consent is what must be given.

stem: The scheme was ___ from the outset: it promised returns that no legitimate investment could produce.
explanationPerOption: Worthy of attention. True but weak, and it does not follow from returns that were impossible.
Correct. If the promised returns were impossible, the collapse could be known in advance, which is what predictable means.
Large in amount. It describes size, not foreseeability.
Having a fault. Closer, but a scheme is not defective in the way a manufactured part is; the colon explains foreseeability, not a flaw in construction.

stem: Only one ___ of the report was released; the remaining chapters stayed classified for a decade.
explanationPerOption: The purpose a thing serves. A report's function is not released chapter by chapter.
Correct. A section is a distinct part of a larger document, which the contrast with 'the remaining chapters' confirms.
Resistance between moving surfaces. It has no textual sense.
The taking of a person by force. Shares the ending only.

stem: The building ___ extensive repair before it could reopen to the public.
explanationPerOption: Took on a task deliberately. A building cannot choose to take on repair; it receives it.
Correct. To undergo something is to experience it passively, which is the building's relation to being repaired.
Weakened gradually from beneath. It would mean the building damaged the repair.
Grasped the meaning of. Buildings do not comprehend.
